note: [2026-10-13] A Docker volume is a mechanism for persisting data generated by and used by Docker containers. It allows data to be stored outside the container’s writable layer, ensuring that data remains even after the container is stopped or removed. Volumes are managed by Docker and are the preferred way to persist data in Docker applications. They can be shared between containers and are independent of the container’s lifecycle. Unlike bind mounts, volumes are fully managed by Docker and offer better performance and portability. Common use cases include database storage, configuration files, and application logs. You create a volume using `docker volume create` and mount it to a container using the `-v` or `--mount` flag when running `docker run`. This ensures data durability and separation of concerns between application logic and data storage.
